# obol.splits

:::caution[v3 release candidate, unreleased]

This is the reference for `@obolnetwork/obol-sdk@3.0.0-rc.12`, generated from its source and spec. Names and shapes may still change before 3.0.0, and it is not on npm `latest`. For the released SDK see the [2.x reference](../../sdk/index.md).

:::

SplitV2 splits: share math in parts per million (`percent`, `splitParams`), deterministic addresses (`predictSplit`), creation, reads, and `prepareDistributeAll`, which distributes an OVM, the splits behind its recipients and the recipients' Warehouse balances in one transaction.

<div class="sdk-table">

| Method | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`percent`](#percent) | A percentage as integer ppm, without float arithmetic: `"33.3333"` and `33.3333` give `333333`. |
| [`formatPercent`](#formatPercent) | The shortest decimal percentage for `ppm` with at most 4 decimals: `333333` → `"33.3333"`, `10000` → `"1"`. |
| [`splitParams`](#splitParams) | SplitV2 parameters from recipients with ppm shares. |
| [`predictSplit`](#predictSplit) | The deterministic (CREATE2) address of a SplitV2 split for these params, owner and salt, and whether it exists already. |
| [`prepareCreateSplit`](#prepareCreateSplit) | Creates a SplitV2 split from recipients and shares (parts per million). |
| [`getSplit`](#getSplit) | null when the address is not a SplitV2 split; throws for read failures. |
| [`prepareDistributeAll`](#prepareDistributeAll) | Distributes an OVM, the SplitV2 splits behind its recipients and the recipients' Warehouse balances in one Multicall3 transaction. |
| [`previewDistributeAll`](#previewDistributeAll) | The reads and amounts of `prepareDistributeAll` without a transaction. |
| [`distributionFromReceipt`](#distributionFromReceipt) | Reads a mined distribution: Warehouse `Withdraw` logs for the native token, SplitMain `Withdrawal` logs and the OVM's `DistributeFunds` log. |
| [`DEFAULT_SPLIT_SALT`](#DEFAULT_SPLIT_SALT) | The salt the SDK creates splits with unless one is given. |
| [`hashSplitParams`](#hashSplitParams) | The SplitV2 `splitHash`: keccak256(abi.encode((address[], uint256[], uint256, uint16))). |
| [`MAX_DISTRIBUTION_INCENTIVE`](#MAX_DISTRIBUTION_INCENTIVE) | SplitV2 stores the distribution incentive as a uint16 (at most 6.5535%). |
| [`RAF_SHARE`](#RAF_SHARE) | The Obol RAF share added to every reward split the presets build (1%). |
| [`splitAmounts`](#splitAmounts) | How a split divides `amount` (SplitV2Lib): the distributor reward (`amount × incentive / 1e6`) comes off first, then each recipient gets `floor(rest × allocation / totalAllocation)`. |
| [`SPLITS_SCALE`](#SPLITS_SCALE) | 100% in SplitV2 allocations: 1% is 10000. |

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.getSplit</summary>

Tag: `api+chain` (state always `chain`). Inputs: `{ address, params: SplitParams?, ovm: Address? }` (the API source
is keyed by OVM, so it is asked only when `ovm` is given; `prepareDistributeAll` passes it). Output: `null` when the
address is not a SplitV2 split (1–2), else `{ address, splitHash: Hash32, owner, paused, balance: bigint,
warehouseBalance: bigint, params: SplitParams | null, paramsSource: Source | "input" | null, blockNumber }`.

1. `getCode(address)` is non-empty and not an EIP-7702 delegation (`0xef0100…`), else `null`. This comes first: a
   precompile (e.g. `0x…02`, SHA-256) has no code but answers every call with 32 non-zero bytes, so "`splitHash()`
   returned non-zero" alone accepts it. (new; 2.16 and the 0xSplits SDK lack it)
2. `splitHash()`, `owner()`, `paused()`, balance and Warehouse balance in one `aggregate3`. A call that reverted (the
   batch itself answered) or a zero `splitHash` → `null`. A read that failed (the code or the batch could not be read)
   is [`CHAIN_READ_FAILED`](../errors.md#CHAIN_READ_FAILED), never `null`. (2.16; rc.3 threw `SPLIT_NOT_FOUND` instead of `null`)
3. Params: the input `params`; else the API (`GET /v1/ovm/:network/:address` lists the params of the OVM's split
   recipients, and a split endpoint may follow); else the chain: the latest `SplitUpdated(Split)` log of the split, or,
   if it never updated, the factory's `SplitCreated(address indexed split, Split splitParams, …)` log with `topic1 =
address` (scanned from the factory deployment block, newest first, as "Log scans"). Whatever the source,
   `keccak256(abi.encode((address[], uint256[], uint256, uint16)))` of the params must equal `splitHash`: for input
   params a mismatch is [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH); an API or log answer that does not match is discarded and the next
   source tried. No matching params → `params: null`, `paramsSource: null` (not an error; `prepareDistributeAll` then
   throws [`SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED) if it needs them).

</details>

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.prepareCreateSplit</summary>

Tag: `chain`. Inputs: `{ recipients: { address, share }[], distributionIncentive: uint? (0), owner: Address? (zero),
salt: Hash32? }`. No RAF share is added here; presets add it.

1. `splitParams` checks.
2. Factory code equals the expected bytecode, else [`CONTRACT_NOT_AVAILABLE`](../errors.md#CONTRACT_NOT_AVAILABLE). (2.15 `isContractAvailable`)
3. `predictSplit`; `exists` → [`SPLIT_ALREADY_EXISTS`](../errors.md#SPLIT_ALREADY_EXISTS) (carries `address`; nothing to send).
4. Recipients whose share could never be withdrawn (3.0.0-rc.12), [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) at `recipients`: one of the
   chain's protocol contracts (`issue: "protocol_contract"`: the SplitsWarehouse, the PullSplit factory, the OVM
   factory, SplitMain, the OWR factory, the batch deposit contract, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7002 and
   EIP-7251 request contracts, the Obol token; checked before any chain read), or the split's own predicted address
   (`issue: "self_recipient"`, checked before [`SPLIT_ALREADY_EXISTS`](../errors.md#SPLIT_ALREADY_EXISTS)). The RAF recipient is a normal recipient.
   `prepareOvmWithSplits` applies the same to each split (path `reward.split.recipients` /
   `principal.split.recipients`), and the presets apply the protocol-contract rule (they know the chain, not the
   address). `predictSplit`, `getSplit` and `prepareDistributeAll` stay permissive: they read splits that exist.

Output: `Prepared<"createSplit">` (preview `{ address, params }`) calling `createSplitDeterministic(params, owner, creator = 0x0, salt)` on the
factory.

[`ovm.prepareDistribute`](./ovm.md#prepareDistribute) is the OVM alone.

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.prepareDistributeAll</summary>

Named `splits.prepareDistribution` / `previewDistribution` until 3.0.0-rc.12 ([`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared) kind `distribution`, preview
`DistributionPreview`): it distributes the OVM, its splits and the recipients' Warehouse balances, where
[`ovm.prepareDistribute`](./ovm.md#prepareDistribute) is the OVM alone.

Tag: `chain`. Inputs:

```
{ ovm: Address?, rewardSplit: SplitParams & { address: Address? }?, principalSplit: (same)?,
  recipients: Address[]?,          # whose balances to withdraw; default every recipient of the splits, the Obol RAF included
  includeRaf: bool? (true),        # false: leave the RAF (the chain's rafRecipient) out of the withdrawal set
  minWithdraw: bigint? (1),        # skip a leg (OVM distribution, split distribution, recipient withdrawal) below this
  distributor: Address?, from: Address? }
```

Reads in two `aggregate3` calls pinned to one block: the OVM first (its recipients name the splits), then the splits
and balances. Vectors `distribution.json` (`routing`, `split_distribution`, `prepare`).
(2.16 `prepareDistributeAll`)

1. At least one of `ovm`, `rewardSplit`, `principalSplit` ([`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)). Split params: allocations match
   recipients in length, non-negative integers, positive sum equal to `totalAllocation`.
2. With `ovm`: provenance as `prepareWithdraw` 3; read balance, `fundsPendingWithdrawal`, `amountOfPrincipalStake`,
   `principalThreshold`, both recipients; failure → [`OVM_READ_FAILED`](../errors.md#OVM_READ_FAILED). Routing as `ObolValidatorManager._distributeFunds`.
3. A split's `address` defaults to the OVM's matching recipient; one given and different from it →
   [`SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT`](../errors.md#SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT); no address and no `ovm` → [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
4. Reward and principal split at the same address: params must hash the same (else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH)); it is
   distributed once with both payouts.
5. An OVM recipient that is a SplitV2 split (as `getSplit` 1–2) and has no params from the input → params from
   `getSplit` 3; none → [`SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED) (its funds would stay undistributed).
6. Each split's on-chain `splitHash` equals the params hash, else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH).
7. A split with something to distribute that is `paused` and not owned by the sender → [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED). Also when the
   owner is the sender but a contract (a Safe): through Multicall3 the split sees Multicall3 as `msg.sender`, so only
   an EOA owner passes the pause, as `tx.origin` (as for Warehouse withdrawals below).
8. Splits with a non-zero `distributionIncentive` need `distributor` (default the sender), else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
   An explicit zero-address `distributor` with such a split is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (`issue: "zero_address"`): the
   incentive would be credited to the zero address (3.0.0-rc.12). Without an incentive the distributor is unused.
9. No calls result → [`NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`](../errors.md#NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE). (2.16 threw this at send)

The RAF is withdrawn by default: withdrawing for it is permissionless and costs the other recipients nothing, and
`minWithdraw` skips dust. When it is not in the withdrawal set (`includeRaf: false`, or `recipients` without it) and
has something in the Warehouse after this distribution, Finding [`RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE`](../warnings.md#RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE) (info) with the `amount`.
(rc.4; rc.3 left it out by default)

[`splits.previewDistributeAll(input)`](./splits.md#previewDistributeAll) runs the same reads and returns `PreviewResult<DistributeAllPreview>` (`{ preview,
checks, blockNumber }`) without throwing for `NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`, for a page that shows greyed-out legs with the button disabled. Other errors
(e.g. [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED)) still throw. A recipient in the withdrawal set whose withdrawal is left out keeps `withdraw:
true` and gets a `skipReason`.

Calls (`aggregate3` on Multicall3, in this order):

1. `distributeFunds()` on the OVM if `distributable ≥ minWithdraw` (`allowFailure: false`).
2. Per split with `distributable ≥ minWithdraw`: `distribute(params, NATIVE_TOKEN, distributor)` (`allowFailure:
false`), where `distributable = max(splitBalance + incoming − 1, 0) + max(warehouseBalance − 1, 0)`.
3. Per withdrawn recipient whose amount (balance after the distributions, minus the 1 wei left) is `≥ minWithdraw`:
   Warehouse `withdraw(owner, NATIVE_TOKEN)` if withdrawals are not paused for it (or it is the transaction origin);
   SplitMain v1 `withdraw(account, 1, [])`. Both `allowFailure: true`: a zero balance or a paused owner reverts that
   call alone.

With the default `minWithdraw = 1` wei every non-empty leg is included (2.16 behaviour). Legs below it are still
listed in the preview with a `skipReason`.

Preview: `{ minWithdraw, ovm?: { address, distributable, principalPayout, rewardPayout, principalRecipient,
rewardRecipient, skipReason? }, splits: { address, kind, distributable, distributorReward, skipReason? }[],
recipients: { address, fromOvm, fromRewardSplit, fromPrincipalSplit, distributorReward, warehouseBalance,
splitMainBalance, withdraw: bool, skipReason?, fromThisDistribution, alreadyWaiting }[] }` (the block is the
[`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared)'s `blockNumber`, not repeated in the preview). A recipient's `distributorReward` is the split distribution
incentives credited to it as the distributor (the sum of the included splits' `distributorReward`), 0 for every other
row. `fromThisDistribution = fromOvm + fromRewardSplit + fromPrincipalSplit + distributorReward`: what this distribution
credits the recipient, withdrawn or not. `alreadyWaiting = warehouseBalance + splitMainBalance`: what was waiting for
it before this transaction, from any split. When its withdrawal is included, the wallet receives `fromOvm`, its
Warehouse balance after the split distributions (`alreadyWaiting`'s Warehouse part plus the split credits) and its
SplitMain v1 balance, each less the 1 wei the contract keeps, for the legs at or above `minWithdraw`. (rc.4 replaced
rc.3's `toWallet`, which mixed the two.) `skipReason` is set exactly when a leg is left out: `"nothing"` (0 after the 1
wei kept), `"dust"` (positive but below `minWithdraw`) or `"paused"` (recipients only: Warehouse withdrawals paused
and the sender cannot bypass it). Each split
recipient gets `floor((distributable − distributorReward) × allocation / totalAllocation)`, with `distributorReward =
floor(distributable × distributionIncentive / 1e6)`; withdrawals leave 1 wei.

Notes:

- Warehouse `withdraw` skips the pause check when `msg.sender` or `tx.origin` is the owner. Through Multicall3 only
  `tx.origin` can match, which is the sender only when the sender is an EOA. For a Safe or other contract sender, the
  pause exemption does not apply: Finding [`RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED`](../warnings.md#RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED) (info) for each skipped recipient, and the
  sender gets no exemption. (new; 2.16 assumed the sender is `tx.origin`)
- After mining, [`splits.distributionFromReceipt(receipt)`](./splits.md#distributionFromReceipt) (pure) reads Warehouse `Withdraw` (native token), SplitMain
  `Withdrawal` and OVM `DistributeFunds` logs, matching each log's emitting address. (2.16 `parseDistributionReceipt`)

### splits.previewDistributeAll {#previewDistributeAll}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">chain</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--since" title="Renamed in 3.0.0-rc.12">rc.12: was splits.previewDistribution</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#distribute">8. Distribute and claim</a></div>

The reads and amounts of `prepareDistributeAll` without a transaction.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.splits.previewDistributeAll(
  input: DistributeAllInput,
): Promise<PreviewResult<DistributeAllPreview>>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>input</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/splits#DistributeAllInput">DistributeAllInput</a></span> |  |
| <code>input.ovm?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>input.rewardSplit?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParamsInput">SplitParamsInput</a> &amp; { address?: string }</span> | The split params; `address` defaults to the OVM's matching recipient. |
| <code>input.principalSplit?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParamsInput">SplitParamsInput</a> &amp; { address?: string }</span> |  |
| <code>input.recipients?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string[]</span> | Whose balances to withdraw; default every recipient of the splits (the Obol RAF included). |
| <code>input.includeRaf?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">boolean</span> | Whether the Obol RAF address (the chain's `rafRecipient`) is withdrawn (default true). Withdrawing it is permissionless and costs the recipients nothing. With `false` it is left out of the withdrawal set, and RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE (info) reports what stays in the Warehouse. |
| <code>input.minWithdraw?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span> | Skip a leg moving less than this (wei, default 1). |
| <code>input.distributor?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | Receives split distribution incentives; default the sender. |
| <code>input.from?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | The sender, for the pause rules; default the wallet account. |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;<a href="./types/send#PreviewResult">PreviewResult</a>&lt;<a href="./types/splits#DistributeAllPreview">DistributeAllPreview</a>&gt;&gt;</span>: `{ preview, checks, blockNumber }`, never a transaction.

**Reports** <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--info" href="../warnings#RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE" title="info">RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE</a>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const { preview } = await obol.splits.previewDistributeAll({ ovm: ovmAddress });
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.prepareDistributeAll (shared section)</summary>

Named `splits.prepareDistribution` / `previewDistribution` until 3.0.0-rc.12 ([`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared) kind `distribution`, preview
`DistributionPreview`): it distributes the OVM, its splits and the recipients' Warehouse balances, where
[`ovm.prepareDistribute`](./ovm.md#prepareDistribute) is the OVM alone.

Tag: `chain`. Inputs:

```
{ ovm: Address?, rewardSplit: SplitParams & { address: Address? }?, principalSplit: (same)?,
  recipients: Address[]?,          # whose balances to withdraw; default every recipient of the splits, the Obol RAF included
  includeRaf: bool? (true),        # false: leave the RAF (the chain's rafRecipient) out of the withdrawal set
  minWithdraw: bigint? (1),        # skip a leg (OVM distribution, split distribution, recipient withdrawal) below this
  distributor: Address?, from: Address? }
```

Reads in two `aggregate3` calls pinned to one block: the OVM first (its recipients name the splits), then the splits
and balances. Vectors `distribution.json` (`routing`, `split_distribution`, `prepare`).
(2.16 `prepareDistributeAll`)

1. At least one of `ovm`, `rewardSplit`, `principalSplit` ([`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)). Split params: allocations match
   recipients in length, non-negative integers, positive sum equal to `totalAllocation`.
2. With `ovm`: provenance as `prepareWithdraw` 3; read balance, `fundsPendingWithdrawal`, `amountOfPrincipalStake`,
   `principalThreshold`, both recipients; failure → [`OVM_READ_FAILED`](../errors.md#OVM_READ_FAILED). Routing as `ObolValidatorManager._distributeFunds`.
3. A split's `address` defaults to the OVM's matching recipient; one given and different from it →
   [`SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT`](../errors.md#SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT); no address and no `ovm` → [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
4. Reward and principal split at the same address: params must hash the same (else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH)); it is
   distributed once with both payouts.
5. An OVM recipient that is a SplitV2 split (as `getSplit` 1–2) and has no params from the input → params from
   `getSplit` 3; none → [`SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED) (its funds would stay undistributed).
6. Each split's on-chain `splitHash` equals the params hash, else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH).
7. A split with something to distribute that is `paused` and not owned by the sender → [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED). Also when the
   owner is the sender but a contract (a Safe): through Multicall3 the split sees Multicall3 as `msg.sender`, so only
   an EOA owner passes the pause, as `tx.origin` (as for Warehouse withdrawals below).
8. Splits with a non-zero `distributionIncentive` need `distributor` (default the sender), else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
   An explicit zero-address `distributor` with such a split is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (`issue: "zero_address"`): the
   incentive would be credited to the zero address (3.0.0-rc.12). Without an incentive the distributor is unused.
9. No calls result → [`NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`](../errors.md#NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE). (2.16 threw this at send)

The RAF is withdrawn by default: withdrawing for it is permissionless and costs the other recipients nothing, and
`minWithdraw` skips dust. When it is not in the withdrawal set (`includeRaf: false`, or `recipients` without it) and
has something in the Warehouse after this distribution, Finding [`RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE`](../warnings.md#RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE) (info) with the `amount`.
(rc.4; rc.3 left it out by default)

`splits.previewDistributeAll(input)` runs the same reads and returns `PreviewResult<DistributeAllPreview>` (`{ preview,
checks, blockNumber }`) without throwing for `NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`, for a page that shows greyed-out legs with the button disabled. Other errors
(e.g. [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED)) still throw. A recipient in the withdrawal set whose withdrawal is left out keeps `withdraw:
true` and gets a `skipReason`.

Calls (`aggregate3` on Multicall3, in this order):

1. `distributeFunds()` on the OVM if `distributable ≥ minWithdraw` (`allowFailure: false`).
2. Per split with `distributable ≥ minWithdraw`: `distribute(params, NATIVE_TOKEN, distributor)` (`allowFailure:
false`), where `distributable = max(splitBalance + incoming − 1, 0) + max(warehouseBalance − 1, 0)`.
3. Per withdrawn recipient whose amount (balance after the distributions, minus the 1 wei left) is `≥ minWithdraw`:
   Warehouse `withdraw(owner, NATIVE_TOKEN)` if withdrawals are not paused for it (or it is the transaction origin);
   SplitMain v1 `withdraw(account, 1, [])`. Both `allowFailure: true`: a zero balance or a paused owner reverts that
   call alone.

With the default `minWithdraw = 1` wei every non-empty leg is included (2.16 behaviour). Legs below it are still
listed in the preview with a `skipReason`.

Preview: `{ minWithdraw, ovm?: { address, distributable, principalPayout, rewardPayout, principalRecipient,
rewardRecipient, skipReason? }, splits: { address, kind, distributable, distributorReward, skipReason? }[],
recipients: { address, fromOvm, fromRewardSplit, fromPrincipalSplit, distributorReward, warehouseBalance,
splitMainBalance, withdraw: bool, skipReason?, fromThisDistribution, alreadyWaiting }[] }` (the block is the
[`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared)'s `blockNumber`, not repeated in the preview). A recipient's `distributorReward` is the split distribution
incentives credited to it as the distributor (the sum of the included splits' `distributorReward`), 0 for every other
row. `fromThisDistribution = fromOvm + fromRewardSplit + fromPrincipalSplit + distributorReward`: what this distribution
credits the recipient, withdrawn or not. `alreadyWaiting = warehouseBalance + splitMainBalance`: what was waiting for
it before this transaction, from any split. When its withdrawal is included, the wallet receives `fromOvm`, its
Warehouse balance after the split distributions (`alreadyWaiting`'s Warehouse part plus the split credits) and its
SplitMain v1 balance, each less the 1 wei the contract keeps, for the legs at or above `minWithdraw`. (rc.4 replaced
rc.3's `toWallet`, which mixed the two.) `skipReason` is set exactly when a leg is left out: `"nothing"` (0 after the 1
wei kept), `"dust"` (positive but below `minWithdraw`) or `"paused"` (recipients only: Warehouse withdrawals paused
and the sender cannot bypass it). Each split
recipient gets `floor((distributable − distributorReward) × allocation / totalAllocation)`, with `distributorReward =
floor(distributable × distributionIncentive / 1e6)`; withdrawals leave 1 wei.

Notes:

- Warehouse `withdraw` skips the pause check when `msg.sender` or `tx.origin` is the owner. Through Multicall3 only
  `tx.origin` can match, which is the sender only when the sender is an EOA. For a Safe or other contract sender, the
  pause exemption does not apply: Finding [`RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED`](../warnings.md#RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED) (info) for each skipped recipient, and the
  sender gets no exemption. (new; 2.16 assumed the sender is `tx.origin`)
- After mining, [`splits.distributionFromReceipt(receipt)`](./splits.md#distributionFromReceipt) (pure) reads Warehouse `Withdraw` (native token), SplitMain
  `Withdrawal` and OVM `DistributeFunds` logs, matching each log's emitting address. (2.16 `parseDistributionReceipt`)

## Pure helpers {#group-helpers}

### splits.percent {#percent}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span></div>

A percentage as integer ppm, without float arithmetic: `"33.3333"` and
`33.3333` give `333333`. Checks: at most three integer digits and four
decimals (no sign, exponent or spaces), result in [1, 1_000_000]; else
PAYLOAD_INVALID.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.splits.percent(p: string | number): bigint
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>p</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string &#124; number</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const share = splits.percent('33.3333'); // 333333n parts per million
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.percent / splits.formatPercent / splits.splitParams (shared section)</summary>

Tag: `pure`. Vectors `split_shares.json`.

- `percent(p: string | number)` → ppm: matches `^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,4})?$`, result in `[1, 1_000_000]`, else
  [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID). No float arithmetic. (2.16 `percentToShares`)
- `formatPercent(ppm)` → the shortest decimal string with at most 4 decimals (`333333` → `"33.3333"`).
- `splitParams(recipients: { address, share: bigint }[], distributionIncentive: uint)` → [`SplitParams`](./types/core.md#SplitParams):
  1. At least one recipient; valid, unique (case-insensitive) addresses, none of them the zero address; shares
     positive integers; sum exactly `1_000_000`. Else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) with `issue` `empty_recipients`,
     `invalid_address`, `zero_address`, `duplicate_address`, `share_not_positive_integer` or `sum_mismatch`. (2.16
     `readShares`, 2.15 float tolerance dropped; `zero_address` new in 3.0.0-rc.12: a share allocated to the zero
     address can never be withdrawn from the Warehouse.) An address is all-lowercase, all-uppercase or a valid
     EIP-55 checksum; a mixed-case one with a wrong checksum is `invalid_address`, never normalised.
  2. `distributionIncentive` ≤ 65535 ([`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)). (2.15 `distributorFeePercent ≤ 6.5535`)
  3. Recipients sorted by numeric address; `totalAllocation` = sum.

### splits.splitParams {#splitParams}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span></div>

SplitV2 parameters from recipients with ppm shares. Checks: at least one
recipient; valid, unique (case-insensitive), non-zero addresses; positive integer
shares summing to exactly 1_000_000; `distributionIncentive` ≤ 65535.
Failures are PAYLOAD_INVALID with an `issue`. Recipients come out sorted by
numeric address, checksummed. No RAF share is added.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.splits.splitParams(
  recipients: ShareRecipient[],
  distributionIncentive?: number,
): SplitParams
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>recipients</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/splits#ShareRecipient">ShareRecipient</a>[]</span> |  |
| <code>distributionIncentive?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParams">SplitParams</a></span>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const params = splits.splitParams([
  { address: '0x5c2f1a8a6a0b3b0ad7a3d8d5f0b6f4c7e2a1b9c3', share: splits.percent(50) },
  { address: '0x9a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f901234567', share: splits.percent(50) },
]);
```

### splits.predictSplit {#predictSplit}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">chain</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 1</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#rewards">2. Withdrawal and reward contracts</a></div>

The deterministic (CREATE2) address of a SplitV2 split for these params, owner and salt,
and whether it exists already.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.splits.predictSplit(
  input: PredictSplitInput,
): Promise<{ address: Address; exists: boolean }>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>input</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/splits#PredictSplitInput">PredictSplitInput</a></span> |  |
| <code>input.params</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParamsInput">SplitParamsInput</a></span> |  |
| <code>input.owner</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | The zero address creates an immutable split. |
| <code>input.salt?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | 32-byte hex; default DEFAULT_SPLIT_SALT. |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;{ address: Address; exists: boolean }&gt;</span>

**Throws** <span class="sdk-muted">(per spec)</span> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#CHAIN_READ_FAILED">CHAIN_READ_FAILED</a> <span class="sdk-muted">plus the [checks every operation runs](../errors.md#checks-every-operation-runs)</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const recipients = [
  { address: '0x5c2f1a8a6a0b3b0ad7a3d8d5f0b6f4c7e2a1b9c3', share: splits.percent(50) },
  { address: '0x9a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f901234567', share: splits.percent(50) },
];
const { address, exists } = await obol.splits.predictSplit({ params: splits.splitParams(recipients), owner: '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' });
```

<summary>Specification: splits.predictSplit</summary>

Tag: `chain`. Inputs: `{ params: SplitParams, owner: Address (zero = immutable), salt: Hash32? }`. Output: `{ address,
exists: bool }` from the factory's `predictDeterministicAddress(params, owner, salt)` and `isDeployed(params, owner,
salt)`. A failed `isDeployed` call is an error (`CHAIN_READ_FAILED`), not `exists: false`. (2.15 treated a failed
check as not deployed)

### splits.distributionFromReceipt {#distributionFromReceipt}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">chain</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#distribute">8. Distribute and claim</a></div>

Reads a mined distribution: Warehouse `Withdraw` logs for the native token,
SplitMain `Withdrawal` logs and the OVM's `DistributeFunds` log. Only logs
emitted by the chain's Warehouse / SplitMain and the given OVM count.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.splits.distributionFromReceipt(
  receipt: DistributionReceipt,
  options?: { ovm?: string },
): DistributionResult
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>receipt</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/splits#DistributionReceipt">DistributionReceipt</a></span> |  |
| <code>receipt.logs</code> | <span class="sdk-type">ReadonlyArray&lt;{ address: string; topics: readonly Hex[]; data: Hex }&gt;</span> |  |
| <code>options?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">{ ovm?: string }</span> |  |
| <code>options.ovm?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/splits#DistributionResult">DistributionResult</a></span>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const paid = obol.splits.distributionFromReceipt(receipt, { ovm: ovmAddress });
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: splits.prepareDistributeAll (shared section)</summary>

Named `splits.prepareDistribution` / `previewDistribution` until 3.0.0-rc.12 ([`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared) kind `distribution`, preview
`DistributionPreview`): it distributes the OVM, its splits and the recipients' Warehouse balances, where
[`ovm.prepareDistribute`](./ovm.md#prepareDistribute) is the OVM alone.

Tag: `chain`. Inputs:

```
{ ovm: Address?, rewardSplit: SplitParams & { address: Address? }?, principalSplit: (same)?,
  recipients: Address[]?,          # whose balances to withdraw; default every recipient of the splits, the Obol RAF included
  includeRaf: bool? (true),        # false: leave the RAF (the chain's rafRecipient) out of the withdrawal set
  minWithdraw: bigint? (1),        # skip a leg (OVM distribution, split distribution, recipient withdrawal) below this
  distributor: Address?, from: Address? }
```

Reads in two `aggregate3` calls pinned to one block: the OVM first (its recipients name the splits), then the splits
and balances. Vectors `distribution.json` (`routing`, `split_distribution`, `prepare`).
(2.16 `prepareDistributeAll`)

1. At least one of `ovm`, `rewardSplit`, `principalSplit` ([`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)). Split params: allocations match
   recipients in length, non-negative integers, positive sum equal to `totalAllocation`.
2. With `ovm`: provenance as `prepareWithdraw` 3; read balance, `fundsPendingWithdrawal`, `amountOfPrincipalStake`,
   `principalThreshold`, both recipients; failure → [`OVM_READ_FAILED`](../errors.md#OVM_READ_FAILED). Routing as `ObolValidatorManager._distributeFunds`.
3. A split's `address` defaults to the OVM's matching recipient; one given and different from it →
   [`SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT`](../errors.md#SPLIT_NOT_OVM_RECIPIENT); no address and no `ovm` → [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
4. Reward and principal split at the same address: params must hash the same (else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH)); it is
   distributed once with both payouts.
5. An OVM recipient that is a SplitV2 split (as `getSplit` 1–2) and has no params from the input → params from
   `getSplit` 3; none → [`SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_REQUIRED) (its funds would stay undistributed).
6. Each split's on-chain `splitHash` equals the params hash, else [`SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PARAMS_MISMATCH).
7. A split with something to distribute that is `paused` and not owned by the sender → [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED). Also when the
   owner is the sender but a contract (a Safe): through Multicall3 the split sees Multicall3 as `msg.sender`, so only
   an EOA owner passes the pause, as `tx.origin` (as for Warehouse withdrawals below).
8. Splits with a non-zero `distributionIncentive` need `distributor` (default the sender), else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).
   An explicit zero-address `distributor` with such a split is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (`issue: "zero_address"`): the
   incentive would be credited to the zero address (3.0.0-rc.12). Without an incentive the distributor is unused.
9. No calls result → [`NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`](../errors.md#NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE). (2.16 threw this at send)

The RAF is withdrawn by default: withdrawing for it is permissionless and costs the other recipients nothing, and
`minWithdraw` skips dust. When it is not in the withdrawal set (`includeRaf: false`, or `recipients` without it) and
has something in the Warehouse after this distribution, Finding [`RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE`](../warnings.md#RAF_LEFT_IN_WAREHOUSE) (info) with the `amount`.
(rc.4; rc.3 left it out by default)

[`splits.previewDistributeAll(input)`](./splits.md#previewDistributeAll) runs the same reads and returns `PreviewResult<DistributeAllPreview>` (`{ preview,
checks, blockNumber }`) without throwing for `NOTHING_TO_DISTRIBUTE`, for a page that shows greyed-out legs with the button disabled. Other errors
(e.g. [`SPLIT_PAUSED`](../errors.md#SPLIT_PAUSED)) still throw. A recipient in the withdrawal set whose withdrawal is left out keeps `withdraw:
true` and gets a `skipReason`.

Calls (`aggregate3` on Multicall3, in this order):

1. `distributeFunds()` on the OVM if `distributable ≥ minWithdraw` (`allowFailure: false`).
2. Per split with `distributable ≥ minWithdraw`: `distribute(params, NATIVE_TOKEN, distributor)` (`allowFailure:
false`), where `distributable = max(splitBalance + incoming − 1, 0) + max(warehouseBalance − 1, 0)`.
3. Per withdrawn recipient whose amount (balance after the distributions, minus the 1 wei left) is `≥ minWithdraw`:
   Warehouse `withdraw(owner, NATIVE_TOKEN)` if withdrawals are not paused for it (or it is the transaction origin);
   SplitMain v1 `withdraw(account, 1, [])`. Both `allowFailure: true`: a zero balance or a paused owner reverts that
   call alone.

With the default `minWithdraw = 1` wei every non-empty leg is included (2.16 behaviour). Legs below it are still
listed in the preview with a `skipReason`.

Preview: `{ minWithdraw, ovm?: { address, distributable, principalPayout, rewardPayout, principalRecipient,
rewardRecipient, skipReason? }, splits: { address, kind, distributable, distributorReward, skipReason? }[],
recipients: { address, fromOvm, fromRewardSplit, fromPrincipalSplit, distributorReward, warehouseBalance,
splitMainBalance, withdraw: bool, skipReason?, fromThisDistribution, alreadyWaiting }[] }` (the block is the
[`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared)'s `blockNumber`, not repeated in the preview). A recipient's `distributorReward` is the split distribution
incentives credited to it as the distributor (the sum of the included splits' `distributorReward`), 0 for every other
row. `fromThisDistribution = fromOvm + fromRewardSplit + fromPrincipalSplit + distributorReward`: what this distribution
credits the recipient, withdrawn or not. `alreadyWaiting = warehouseBalance + splitMainBalance`: what was waiting for
it before this transaction, from any split. When its withdrawal is included, the wallet receives `fromOvm`, its
Warehouse balance after the split distributions (`alreadyWaiting`'s Warehouse part plus the split credits) and its
SplitMain v1 balance, each less the 1 wei the contract keeps, for the legs at or above `minWithdraw`. (rc.4 replaced
rc.3's `toWallet`, which mixed the two.) `skipReason` is set exactly when a leg is left out: `"nothing"` (0 after the 1
wei kept), `"dust"` (positive but below `minWithdraw`) or `"paused"` (recipients only: Warehouse withdrawals paused
and the sender cannot bypass it). Each split
recipient gets `floor((distributable − distributorReward) × allocation / totalAllocation)`, with `distributorReward =
floor(distributable × distributionIncentive / 1e6)`; withdrawals leave 1 wei.

Notes:

- Warehouse `withdraw` skips the pause check when `msg.sender` or `tx.origin` is the owner. Through Multicall3 only
  `tx.origin` can match, which is the sender only when the sender is an EOA. For a Safe or other contract sender, the
  pause exemption does not apply: Finding [`RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED`](../warnings.md#RECIPIENT_WITHDRAW_PAUSED) (info) for each skipped recipient, and the
  sender gets no exemption. (new; 2.16 assumed the sender is `tx.origin`)
- After mining, `splits.distributionFromReceipt(receipt)` (pure) reads Warehouse `Withdraw` (native token), SplitMain
  `Withdrawal` and OVM `DistributeFunds` logs, matching each log's emitting address. (2.16 `parseDistributionReceipt`)

</details>

### splits.hashSplitParams {#hashSplitParams}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

The SplitV2 `splitHash`: keccak256(abi.encode((address[], uint256[], uint256, uint16))).

```ts sdk-signature
splits.hashSplitParams(params: SplitParams): Hex
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>params</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParams">SplitParams</a></span> |  |

| <code>params.totalAllocation</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Hex</span>

**Example**


### splits.splitAmounts {#splitAmounts}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

How a split divides `amount` (SplitV2Lib): the distributor reward
(`amount × incentive / 1e6`) comes off first, then each recipient gets
`floor(rest × allocation / totalAllocation)`. Vectors `split_distribution`.

```ts sdk-signature
splits.splitAmounts(
  params: SplitParams,
  amount: bigint,
): { amounts: bigint[]; distributorReward: bigint }
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>params</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#SplitParams">SplitParams</a></span> |  |
| <code>params.recipients</code> | <span class="sdk-type">Address[]</span> |  |
| <code>params.allocations</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint[]</span> |  |
| <code>params.totalAllocation</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span> |  |
| <code>params.distributionIncentive</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> | Parts per million (uint16 on chain, so at most 65535). |
| <code>amount</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">{ amounts: bigint[]; distributorReward: bigint }</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { splits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';
import { parseEther } from 'viem';

const twoWay = splits.splitParams([
  { address: '0x5c2f1a8a6a0b3b0ad7a3d8d5f0b6f4c7e2a1b9c3', share: 500_000 },
  { address: '0x9a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f901234567', share: 500_000 },
]);
const { amounts, distributorReward } = splits.splitAmounts(twoWay, parseEther('1'));
```
